## On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Status:** Ongoing / unresolved (still failing as of the last log entry)

**Impact window:** 2026-03-14 02:14:18Z → at least 03:59:27Z (end of available log; incident had not recovered — `waiting` queue depth was still climbing, from 13 to 74)

**Root cause:** `dep-4471` (gateway, deployed by a.novak, 02:12:00Z–02:14:00Z) — *"config: connection-per-request for pool isolation"*. It flipped `gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true` (config generation 118→119, applied 02:13:41Z). This drove connection demand past the fixed pool cap of 20, and the pool never drained. Every failure logs `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting N)` — first hit at 02:14:18.972Z, ~37s after the config applied.

**Scope:** Gateway only. All four backends behind it (billing-svc, orders-svc, catalog-svc, accounts-svc) are 503ing equally, confirming it's the gateway's connection pool, not an upstream/DB outage. Workers (`logs/worker.log`) are unaffected — no errors, jobs completing normally throughout on their own separate DB pool — ruling out a shared infra problem.

**Action: roll back `dep-4471`** (revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false`, or redeploy the prior gateway config generation 118). No other deploy in the window is implicated — `dep-4472` (billing-svc, 02:41Z) and `dep-4473` (catalog-svc, 03:20Z) are per-service and post-date the onset; they don't explain the gateway-wide, simultaneous failure pattern.

**Next check after rollback:** watch `pool.stats` lines for `waiting` returning to 0 and `in_use` dropping below 20; confirm 503 rate drops to zero, not just slows.
